text: My dear students I am fully convinced that you are the future architects of a prosperous Pakistan. If you want a thriving Pakistan then it has to be a knowledge based Pakistan. You therefore enter the University to seek knowledge and leave to disseminate knowledge. In today's world high expectations and demands are placed on the centres of higher st education. The 21 century calls for new approaches to learning and innovative thinking. The acquisition of specific knowledge not just about the discipline that they belong to but also about the environment, health and citizenship will hone their ethical values and attitudes. In our rapidly changing and interdependent world, the universities not only have to ensure that students acquire solid skills in basic subjects, but also that they become responsible local and global citizens, at ease with new technologies and able to make informed decisions about local and global challenges. Going global is the recipe to international peace, harmony and prosperity. Furthermore, remember one thing; education and all its forms crown those who nurture her. text: The City-Multan The City-Multan Multan, the city of saints, has been a center of learning, culture and civilization for centuries . It is one of the oldest living cities of the world. Its original name as described by Hiuen Tsang, a Chinese traveller, who visited the city in October 641 A.D., was ‘Mu- lo-san-pu-lu’, which is believed to be a translation of ‘Mulasthana-Pura’. Al-Beruni, who came to South Asia in 1015 A.D. alongwith his Master Sultan Mahmud Ghaznavi, writes about the town as ‘Mulatana’. He visited Multan the same year and recorded that Multan was originally called ‘Kasyapapura, then Hansapura, then Bhagapura, then Sambapura and then Mulasthana. Sir Gen. Alexander Cunningham, after conducting excavations in the old fort in 1853 A.D. and 1864 A.D., further adds to these names those of ‘Prahladapura and Adysthana’. The first recorded event in the history is the invasion of Alexander the Great in February 325 B.C. Several other important historians visited Multan including Masudi (915 A.D.), Istakhri (951 A.D.) and Ibn Batuta (1334 A.D.) and they all wrote about the social, cultural and educational activities in Multan. Multan’s importance has always been acknowledged an

Multan’s importance has always been acknowledged and it has always maintained its distinguished and honorable position among the cities of this region. The city (740 ft. above sea level) is located almost in the center of Pakistan. It is at a distance of approximately 950 km from Karachi and 630 km from Islamabad, right on the main highway and about six kilometers from the mighty Chenab, in a bend created by the five confluent rivers. The vast plain of Multan Division is dissected by rivers, canals and narrow water channels, forming an ideal agricultural base for the economic development of the region.

title: Page 17
text: The University The University Multan has always remained a centre of excellence in education. Hazrat Bahauddin Zakariya (1172 - 1262 A.D.), a Muslim religious scholar and saint, established a school of higher learning in theology in Multan; where scholars from all over the world came for studies and research. Multan has maintained its central position and centuries old cultural heritage and therefore suited ideally to become a center of learning. Thus the University of Multan was established in 1975 by an Act of the Punjab Legislative Assembly. To pay homage to the Great Saint, the name was changed from University of Multan to Bahauddin Zakariya University in 1979. The University is located at a distance of 10 km from the city center. The main Campus is spread over 960 acres of land. The University has a fleet of 42 buses for the Commute facility to students and staff. The University started functioning in 1975 in rented buildings with 8 departments. Presently, it has more than 40 departments/institutes/colleges. text: Library plays a vital role in the academic life of a university. The fundamental role of the library is educational. It should not be operated as a mere store house of books rather it should be dynamic instrument of education. The Central Library of the university is being organized on these lines. The library collections support not only every course in the curriculum but also include selected stocks of journal, Reference books, Periodicals, Publications and newspaper etc. Most of the departments have their own departmental library situated in their buildings. The total number of books of the Central Library and departmental libraries is approximately 300000. The library administration is vested in the library committee which is responsible for efficient management of the library system. The University library is being computerized and online library services through University OPAC (Online Public Access Catalogue) available through network. Other online resources like Research Catalogue, Peer reviewed Journals, Pakistan Research Repository, IEEE Engineering database, Agricultural Research links and HEC Digital Library access also offer on campus network. title: Page 20
text: The University, at present, has seven hostels for boys and eight hostels for girls. In all the hostels, the residents are provided with the necessary facilities. Internet facility is also provided in the hostels. The mess is run by students. The places in these hostels are filled on the recommendation of the Chairpersons of respective departments. The students, desirous of staying in the hostel, are, therefore, advised to submit their applications, in quadruplicate, to the office of the Chairman Hall Council through the Chairman/Chairperson of their respective Department. Seats available in the hostels are limited. So hostel facility cannot be claimed as a matter of right. It is privilege. Allotment in the hostels will be on merit as per “Hostel Accommodation” rules and regulation. Hostels are designated and attached with departments. Change of hostel will not be allowed in any case. Accommodation Consultation and advisory health services are available for the students. A reasonably equipped dispensary, looked after by two senior doctors and assisted by qualified staff, exists at the campus. Complicated cases are referred to the specialists in the Nishtar Hospital, Multan and CPI I

Note: Misuse of ambulance is strictly prohibited. Students involved in misusing the ambulance will be liable for disciplinary action. text: ORIC was formally established in 2014 in BZU as per the guidelines of Higher Education Commission (HEC) Pakistan with a view point to develop research culture and to promote commercialization of research by translating new ideas into new products and services for National and International industry. Recently, a state-of-the-art new building for ORIC has been constructed in the University where trained staff is working efficiently for escalation of research. BZU, as a growing public sector university of South Punjab remains deeply concerned on promoting research, innovation and commercialization as part of its educational mission.The ORIC-BZU, being anessential body in assisting the University's research, predominantly focuses upon providing strategic and operational support to the entire research network in the campus to achieve desired research outcomes. Furthermore, ORIC at BZU intends to bring BZ University research standards at par with International Universities to meet the most demanding task of ensuring national economic stabilization and prosperity coupled with transforming Pakistan into a knowledge-based economy in this fast paced and competitive world. Transforming resear

ORIC-BZU understands the core values of academic freedom, professional integrity and ethical conduct alongside significance of today's knowledge-driven economy that can help transmute Pakistan into an economic power of the region. text: r. Tahir Sultan Background In 1975, the Government of the Punjab decided to set up four Engineering Colleges at Taxila, Multan, Faisalabad and Bahawalpur in the same order of priority. In accordance with the decision of the Punjab Cabinet, the first Engineering College initially started functioning at Sahiwal and was later, in 1978, shifted to Taxila as a second campus of the University of Engineering and Technology, Lahore. Later its status was raised to an independent University of Engineering and Technology. The proposal for the second College of Engineering and Technology at Multan met the approval of the ECNEC in September 1990. The College of Engineering and Technology was thus established as a Constituent College of the Bahauddin Zakariya University, Multan. In Faculty of Engineering & Technology 2019 its status upgrated to faculty of Engineering & Technology. Its broad objective is to produce engineers at undergraduate level with Bachelor’s degree in conventional fields of Civil, Building & Architectural, Electrical, Computer, Mechanical, Metallurgy & Materials and Textile Engineering to meet the engineering manpower requirements of the province/country. text: 90 Prospectus Year 2024 Introduction The Department of Building & Architectural Engineering was established in Baha Ud-din Zakariya University in 2004. Initially it offered 5-year BSc Building & Architectural Engineering Program. However, in 2009, the program duration was reduced to 4-year to comply with the Pakistan Engineering Council (PEC) requirements. Since then the department is offering 4-year BSc program in Building & Architectural Engineering. The Building & Architectural Engineering program is a blend of Architecture and Civil Engineering with emphasis to impart quality education to the students and prepare them for the building industry of Pakistan. The graduates of our department are working in various national and international organizations. The curriculum of the program is designed to equip the graduates with architectural design, building structural design, building services design (e.g. HVAC systems, electrical systems in buildings, lighting & illumination, fire safety, acoustics and plumbing) with strong knowledge of construction materials, construction techniques, construction management and conservation of heritage buildings. text: 111 Prospectus Year 2024 Institute of Sufism & Mysticism Sufism, also known as Tasawwuf, a mystical dimension of Islam. It emerged in the 8th century CE, primarily in present-day Iran, Iraq, and Central Asia.Sufism and Mysticism have a rich history that spans over 1,400 years, with roots in Islamic spirituality. Early Sufis sought a more personal and intimate connection with Allah.Sufism emphasizes the importance of spiritual guidance, meditation, contemplation, and devotional rituals and commitment to ethical and moral values. The ultimate goal is to become a true servant of Almighty ALLAH, living a life of love, compassion and service to all of his creations. The Institute of Sufism & Mysticism Bahauddin Zakariya University, Multan attempts to promote a moderate and responsible style of discourse on the issues concerning contemporary understanding of Islam and the challenges that are faced by the humanity in general and Muslim World in particular.The Institute pays special attention to developing contact with relevant scholars and institutions across the globe for advancing research and studies in the field. Soon it was converted into the Department of Saraiki in May 2006, and the regular classes of M.A. Saraiki were started accordingly. The Saraiki Region, being a part of the vast area of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization, owns rich traditions of language, literature, culture, history and archaeology etc. Saraiki is the ancient native language of the Southern Punjab and several districts of Sindh, Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with centuries old shared traditions of literature and cultural activities. The ex-Prime-Minister Syed Yousuf Raza Gillani inaugurated the Saraiki Area Study Centre on 23rd January 2010. A commemorative book “Saraiki Wasaib” was also published on this occasion. It is worth mentioning that following four new academic departments have been also approved in the scheme of SASC: 1. Initially, it was housed in a rented building but later on it was shifted to a part of a borrowed building at Bosan Road, Multan. The Department shifted to its present premises at the University Campus in 1984. A three years course for the degree of B.Pharmacy was launched in 1976 which was then replaced by a four year course in 1979 on the recommendations of the University Grants Commission (Now HEC). text: ). B.Pharmacy (four year program) has now been replaced by a five year Program of Pharm.D. from the session 2003-2004. The Department after its establishment, gradually strengthened its academic program as a result of which in 1992, it was given the status of a separate Faculty of Pharmacy. This subject has gathered a high reputation all around the world due to its applied nature. Environmental science is a cosmopolitan subject because it deals with various disciplines like chemistry, physics, botany, zoology, geology, geograph

title: Page 145
text: on all around the world due to its applied nature. Environmental science is a cosmopolitan subject because it deals with various disciplines like chemistry, physics, botany, zoology, geology, geography, and public health etc. It focuses on the sources, reactions, transport, effects and fate of physical and biological species in the air, water and soil along with the effects of human activity upon these. Air, water, land, and noise pollution constantly imperil quality of life and damage the pristine environment. World today is facing serious environmental crisis, for instance, increase in the heat budget of the earth, depletion of non-renewable resources, air pollution, pollution of surface & ground waters, heavy metal pollution, massive destruction of habitats, deforestation, mining, over-fishing and radiation pollution. Ecosystem of earth is very fragile, and man’s tampering with it may, in the end, make the earth unlivable, not only for man but for all life forms. Environmental pollution drastically reduces the productivity of plants, and is primarily involved in causing several illnesses to the humans: ranging from breathing disorders, cancer, stomach upset, skin allergies, card

title: Page 145
text: tion drastically reduces the productivity of plants, and is primarily involved in causing several illnesses to the humans: ranging from breathing disorders, cancer, stomach upset, skin allergies, cardiovascular problems, neurobehavioral ailments, kidney damage, typhoid, hepatitis, and most of the enteric & diarrheal diseases due to transmittance of microorganisms via the contaminated water. text: 165 Prospectus Year 2024 Department of Soil Science Department of Soil Science Introduction The Department of Soil Science is one of the main departments of the Faculty of Agricutural Sciences and Technology. The Department of Soil Science provides the students with a professional development in the field of Soil Science and water Management. Soil is a vital part of the natural environment; essential for life. Soil serves as the medium for plant growth, habitat for many organisms, filtration system for surface water and storage of atmospheric carbon. Therefore, it influences the distribution, population and health of plant and animal species. Soil produces food, feed and fiber for us. Agricutural production of a farm is largely dependent on quality of its soil. Soil Science is an applied science and faculty members are working on developing sustainable strategies and technologies that solve problem associated with soils as a medium for plant growth. The core activities of the department are centered at teaching, research and extension of innovations in soil, fertilizer and water sciences. Research and teaching laboratories of the Department are equipped with sophisticated equipment

Class rooms and laboratories of the Department are well managed to train the students in soil physics, soil chemistry, soil microbiology and biochemistry, soil fertility and plant nutrition. text: 167 Prospectus Year 2024 Department of Agricultural Engineering Department of Agricultural Engineering Introduction The Department of Agricultural Engineering was established at University College of Agriculture, Bahauddin Zakariya University, Multan in 2004. text: 188 Prospectus Year 2024 Department of Food Safety & Quality Management Introduction The Department of Food Safety & Quality Management is the first and only department in South Punjab offering comprehensive BS and MS degree programs as well as distinguished PhD program, dedicate to the field of food safety & quality management. In today’s world, food safety has emerged as a paramount concern for consumers worldwide. Recognizing this pressing need, governments and regulatory agencies have placed significant emphasis on enhancing food safety standards. Our department aims to address this critical global demand by providing exceptional educational opportunities and training in the dynamic field of food safety and quality management. Our carefully designed curriculum equips students with the knowledge, skills, and expertise necessary to navigate the complexities of the food industry, ensuring the highest standards of safety and quality. Food safety and quality management is a vital area of research that holds relevance for all food industries across the globe. Professionals specializing in food safety play a pivotal role in ensuring the highest standards of safety and quality within t

title: Page 183
text: f research that holds relevance for all food industries across the globe. Professionals specializing in food safety play a pivotal role in ensuring the highest standards of safety and quality within these industries. In fact, the field of food safety has become one of the largest job sectors worldwide. Graduates with expertise in food safety and quality management find themselves employed as esteemed food safety and quality experts in a diverse range of establishments, including hotels, restaurants, bakeries, confectionary industries, fats and oil industries, dairy industries, cereal industries, and many others. Their responsibilities encompass the implementation of stringent food safety standards and working tirelessly to enhance the safety and quality of various food commodities. These dedicated professionals work tirelessly, day and night, to safeguard consumer health and wellbeing by maintaining the integrity of our food supply. Objectives a. text: 203 Prospectus Year 2024 INTODUCTION Lodhran is a city about 80 km away in the southern side of Multan and is the headquarter of District in the Punjab Province of Pakistan. The city is located on the northern side of river Satluj. In its north, the Districts of Multan and Khanewal are located while in its East side is neighbored by Vehari whereas Bahawalpur is on its southern side and West side is bordered by Jalalpur Peer Wala (District Multan). District Lodhran is spread over an area of 1,790 square kilometers comprising of following three Tehsils: Lodhran, Dunyapur and Kahror Pakka. Lodhran was made District Headquarter on 1st July 1991; by the Government of Punjab vide Notification No.(30-06-91) 565-91/490 Ros-SO-II, while its town committee was upgraded in 1992 vide Notification No. SO-V/LG 535/91. The District was the hometown and political arena to Muhammad Siddique Khan Kanju, (Ex-Minister of State for Foreign Affairs) during Nawaz Sharif’s government in 1990. It was due to his initiative that Lodhran was made a District in 1991. In the same year, when Tehsil Lodhran was upgraded as a District, it had 436 villages or Mauzas, 14 more were included in the district in 1992 by

title: Page 195
text: s initiative that Lodhran was made a District in 1991. In the same year, when Tehsil Lodhran was upgraded as a District, it had 436 villages or Mauzas, 14 more were included in the district in 1992 by detaching them from Tehsil Jalal PurPirwala (District Multan), through the orders of Punjab Government No. 180-92/C- 65/703 SO-II dated 25-06-1992. Being a District Headquarter, it was divided into three Tehsil. Now, the prestigious Lodhran District comprises of 3 tehsil and 73 union councils, of which 11 are urban and 62, are rural UCs. The height of the District Lodhran from the sea level is about 380 feet. The District Lodhran is laying between the river Satluj and the Bias. The city’s location makes it strategically important in Southern Punjab yet it is still considered as under developed in terms of administrative and commercial affairs. It is one of the central cities which connect Punjab to Sindh. Railway double track was initially started from Lodhran to Karachi but now it was extended to Lahore. title: BZU Prospectus 2026 - PDF Page 9
text:
Source: Bahauddin Zakariya University Prospectus Year 2026, physical PDF page 9.
Dear Future Leaders,
Welcome to Bahauddin Zakariya University, Multan, recognized globally by Times Higher Education Rankings and
QS World Rankings for our academic excellence and research contributions. You are not merely exploring
educational opportunities. You are embarking on a transformative journey that will shape your destiny and Pakistan's
future. At BZU, we transcend traditional learning boundaries. Our institution forges brilliant minds where intellectual
curiosity meets practical application, and tomorrow's change-makers discover their true potential. We cultivate global
citizens who will lead Pakistan into a new era of prosperity and progress.
The 21st century demands wisdom, adaptability, and innovative thinking across diverse fields. Our world-class faculty
and cutting-edge research facilities in Computer Science, Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence, Data
Science, Business Sciences, Agriculture, and Chemistry provide you with the tools to not only master your chosen
field but to revolutionize it. Whether you aspire to lead the digital transformation through AI and data analytics, drive
agricultural innovation for food security, advance chemical research for sustainable solutions, or excel in business
sciences for economic growth, BZU offers the perfect launching pad for your ambitions.
Our commitment extends beyond academic excellence to nurturing ethical leaders who understand their
responsibility to society. We celebrate the rich diversity of cultures and perspectives that foster mutual respect and
collaborative learning, preparing you for success in our globalized world.
At Bahauddin Zakariya University, we don't just offer education. We deliver transformation. We don't just provide
degrees. We forge destinies. Join us in building a knowledge-driven Pakistan where innovation thrives, excellence is
the standard, and every graduate becomes a catalyst for positive change.
Your journey to greatness begins here.
Dr. Muhammad Zubair Iqbal (SFAHE)
Vice Chancellor
Bahauddin Zakariya University, Multan
Vice Chancellor's Message

title: BZU Prospectus 2026 - PDF Page 10
text:
Source: Bahauddin Zakariya University Prospectus Year 2026, physical PDF page 10.
It is a privilege and an honor to serve as the Chairperson of the Punjab Higher Education Commission (PHEC),
an institution dedicated to advancing the quality, accessibility, and relevance of higher education across the
province of Punjab.
Higher education must play a transformative role—not only in cultivating skilled human capital but also in
generating knowledge, fostering innovation, and promoting equity and inclusion. Our universities must evolve into
dynamic hubs of research, critical thinking, and community engagement centers to address local challenges and
global demands.
My vision for PHEC is to transform higher education institutes into smart and inclusive ecosystems that nurture
knowledge, skills, and values for employability and responsible citizenship, while aligning university research and
innovation with the real needs of society and global best practices.
The Commission will continue to work closely with universities, policymakers, and international partners to
strengthen governance, ensure quality, and foster an ecosystem of innovation. Together, we will uphold merit,
encourage academic freedom, and support initiatives that promote lifelong learning rooted in debate and
dialogue.
I invite all stakeholders–students, faculty, administrators, and partners—to join us in this mission. Together we can
build a resilient and future-ready higher education system that contributes meaningfully to the progress and
prosperity of our society at large.
Prof. Dr. Iqrar Ahmad Khan(HI,SI)
Chairperson PHEC’s Message

world.

The City-Multan	The City-Multan
Multan, the city of saints, has been a center of learning, culture and civilization for centuries . It is one of the oldest living cities of
the world. Its original name as described by Hiuen Tsang, a Chinese traveller, who visited the city in October 641 A.D., was ‘Mu-
lo-san-pu-lu’, which is believed to be a translation of ‘Mulasthana-Pura’. Al-Beruni, who came to South Asia in 1015 A.D.
alongwith his Master Sultan Mahmud Ghaznavi, writes about the town as ‘Mulatana’. He visited Multan the same year and
recorded that Multan was originally called ‘Kasyapapura, then Hansapura, then Bhagapura, then Sambapura and then
Mulasthana. Sir Gen. Alexander Cunningham, after conducting excavations in the old fort in 1853 A.D. and 1864 A.D., further
adds to these names those of ‘Prahladapura and Adysthana’. The first recorded event in the history is the invasion of Alexander the
Great in February 325 B.C.
Several other important historians visited Multan including Masudi (915 A.D.), Istakhri (951 A.D.) and Ibn Batuta (1334 A.D.)
and they all wrote about the social, cultural and educational activities in Multan. Multan’s importance has always been
acknowledged and it has always maintained its distinguished and honorable position among the cities of this region.
The city (740 ft. above sea level) is located almost in the center of Pakistan. It is at a distance of approximately 950 km from
Karachi and 630 km from Islamabad, right on the main highway and about six kilometers from the mighty Chenab, in a bend
created by the five confluent rivers. The vast plain of Multan Division is dissected by rivers, canals and narrow water channels,
forming an ideal agricultural base for the economic development of the region.

title: BZU Prospectus 2026 - PDF Page 19
text:
Source: Bahauddin Zakariya University Prospectus Year 2026, physical PDF page 19.
The University	The University
Multan has always remained a centre of excellence in
education. Hazrat Bahauddin Zakariya (1172 - 1262 A.D.), a
Muslim religious scholar and saint, established a school of
higher learning in theology in Multan; where scholars from all
over the world came for studies and research. Multan has
maintained its central position and centuries old cultural
heritage and therefore suited ideally to become a center of
learning. Thus the University of Multan was established in
1975 by an Act of the Punjab Legislative Assembly. To pay
homage to the Great Saint, the name was changed from
University of Multan to Bahauddin Zakariya University in
1979.
The University is located at a distance of 10 km from the city
center. The main Campus is spread over 960 acres of land. The
University has a fleet of 42 buses for the Commute facility to
students and staff. The University started functioning in 1975
in rented buildings with 8 departments. Presently, it has more
than 40 departments/institutes/colleges. Out of its 599 faculty
members, 333 hold doctoral degrees and among its around
25,160 students, half are female.
The University offers a wide range of programs; B.S., BS 5th
semester MBA, MCS, M.Phil, and Ph.D. in Sciences,
Commerce, Business, Pharmacy, Engineering, Social
Sciences, Agricultural, Veterinary Sciences and Islamic
Studies & Languages. Various short-time courses and
diplomas have become popular with the general public and are
offered from time to time.

Guidelines for Hostel Allotment through the Online Hostel
Management System (HMS)
To facilitate students and ensure transparency, all hostel allotments
at Bahauddin Zakariya University (BZU), Multan, are processed
exclusively through the Online Hostel Management System
(HMS). Students are advised to carefully follow the instructions
given below.
1. Access the Student Portal
Visit the BZU Student Portal at:
portal.bzu.edu.pk
2. Login Using Your Official BZU Email
!· Use the official BZU student email address provided by your
department at the time of admission or received in your
personal email inbox.
!· Enter your BZU email address and the password provided with
the account.Example:
xxxxx@student.bzu.edu.pk
3. Forgot Your Password?
If you have forgotten your password:
! Click on the "Forgot Password" option available on the login page.
! A password reset link or verification code will be sent to your registered email address.
! Reset your password and log in again using the new credentials.
4. Access the Hostel Management System (HMS)
After successful login:
! Click on the "HMS" (Hostel Management System) icon available on the student dashboard.
! Select "Create Request" to initiate your hostel application.
5 Select Request Type: From the Request Type drop-down menu, select:"Request for Hostel"
6 Complete the Hostel Application Form
Fill in all required information carefully and accurately, including:
! Student information
! Parent/Guardian details
! Emergency contact information
! Visitor information (mandatory and restricted to blood relatives only)
! Any additional information requested by the system
Incomplete or incorrect applications may not be processed.
7. Review and Submit the Application
· Carefully review all entered information before submission.
· Click "Create Request" to submit your hostel application online.
8. Track the Status of Your Application
Students can monitor the progress of their hostel application through the HMS portal.
The application status may appear as:
! Submitted
! Allocated
! Rejected
9. Payment of Hostel Dues
! Upon approval and hostel allocation, the required fee vouchers will be generated automatically in the student's HMS
portal.
! Students may download the vouchers and pay the dues:
! Online through the available banking channels, or
! By visiting the designated bank branch in person.

ORIC was formally established in 2014 in BZU as per the guidelines of Higher Education
Commission (HEC) Pakistan with a view point to develop research culture and to promote
commercialization of research by translating new ideas into new products and services for
National and International industry. Recently, a state-of-the-art new building for ORIC has been
constructed in the University where trained staff is working efficiently for escalation of research.
BZU, as a growing public sector university of South Punjab remains deeply concerned on
promoting research, innovation and commercialization as part of its educational mission.The
ORIC-BZU, being anessential body in assisting the University's research, predominantly focuses
upon providing strategic and operational support to the entire research network in the campus to
achieve desired research outcomes. Furthermore, ORIC at BZU intends to bring BZ University
research standards at par with International Universities to meet the most demanding task of
ensuring national economic stabilization and prosperity coupled with transforming Pakistan into a
knowledge-based economy in this fast paced and competitive world. Transforming research
results from the laboratory into new or improved products and services in the marketplace to
engender regional and national economy, is the prime agenda of ORIC-BZU. ORIC-BZU
understands the core values of academic freedom, professional integrity and ethical conduct
alongside significance of today's knowledge-driven economy that can help transmute Pakistan into
an economic power of the region.
Prof. Dr. M. Najam-ul-Haq is performing duties as Director ORIC. He received PhD in Chemistry
with field of specialization in Analytical Chemistry from University of Innsbruck, Austria. The
research was directed towards Development of Carbon Nanomaterials for Protein Immobilization
and Profiling by MALDI-MS. The Post-Doctoral period 2013-2014 was devoted to Development
of Selective Enrichment and Desalting methodologies based on Nano- and Micro-Materials of
varying properties and the subsequent analysis by MALDI-MS. Prof. Najam is one of the leaders
of Nano- and Micro-Materials Chemistry Research at Institute of Chemical Science, Bahauddin
Zakariya University Multan. He worked as Chairman Department of Biochemistry, Bahauddin

Further:
5. COMPLAINTS AND REPORTING
In accordance with the provision under Clause:
5.1 A complaint may be lodged by any person who has experienced sexual harassment as defined in Section 2 (Prohibited
Conduct) read with Section 3 (Jurisdiction) of this policy, with either the Focal Person or with any member of the Sexual
Harassment Inquiry Committee.
5.2 In cases in which the conduct in question falls within the scope of the 2010 Harassment Act, the affected person shall
also have an option to submit a complaint to the Ombudsperson in accordance with the provisions of the 2010 Harassment
Act.
5.3 In the event that a complainant is reluctant to contact the Focal Persons or any members of the Inquiry Committee, the
complainant may contact a colleague, instructor, the employment supervisor, manager, department chair, dean or VC. It
will be the responsibility of the individual contacted to report the case to the appropriate authority.
5.4
Complainants shall be encouraged to submit complaints promptly, preferably within 3 months but no later than 12 months
from the last date of the alleged harassment. An extension of up to 1 year may be granted by the Focal Persons or the
Inquiry Committee upon written request stating the reasons for the delay in submitting the complaint.
5.5
All members of the HEI community are encouraged to report any instances of sexual harassment that they may have
observed to the Focal Persons or the Inquiry Committee. For the purposes of safeguarding the campus community, HEIs
have an obligation to investigate material violations of this policy even in the event that a formal complaint has not been
filed.
5.6
As soon as a complaint or report is received by one of the designated resources, it shall be shared by him or her (within a
period of 24 hours) with all Focal Persons and members of the Inquiry Committee for further action.
5.7
For minor violations, complainants may opt to make an informal complaint to either the Focal Person or the Inquiry

Our vision is to cultivate and disseminate profound knowledge in the
field of Economics to inspire innovative solutions for sustainable
development, shaping a better future for Pakistan and the world.
We aim to advance knowledge and understanding of economics
through exceptional education, impactful research, and community
engagement. By offering innovative and responsive educational
programs at both the undergraduate and graduate levels, we seek to
address local, national, and global economic needs. Our focus is on
delivering real-time, practical solutions to complex economic
challenges through collaborative learning, adaptive teaching methods,
and a commitment to sustainable development. We foster critical
thinking, analytical skills, and ethical values, empowering students
and scholars to contribute to policy innovation and promote inclusive
development. Our pride lies in our culture of academic excellence,
professionalism, and our dedication to producing socially responsible
graduates who are prepared to lead with integrity and make a positive
impact on both Pakistan and the global community.
 To deliver high-quality, innovative, and research-informed
education at undergraduate and graduate levels to build strong
foundations in economic theory and application.
 To encourage impactful and interdisciplinary research that
addresses local, national, and global economic challenges,
fostering policy-relevant solutions for sustainable
development.
 To cultivate critical thinking, analytical capabilities, and ethical
values among students and scholars to prepare them for
leadership in economic policy, academia, and industry.
 To strengthen community engagement and industry
partnerships to enhance the social relevance and real-world
application of economic knowledge and skills.
 To integrate sustainability and inclusivity into all aspects of
academic and institutional operations to contribute meaningfully
to Pakistan’s and the world’s development goals.
 To equip students with the skills, mindset, and professional
ethics to thrive in diverse global contexts and contribute to the
global economy with responsibility and impact.

The Department of History was established in 1976, a year after the
establishment of the University. Initially, the Department started
functioning in a rented building in Gulgasht Colony, Multan. In 1980,
it was shifted to Languages Block and finally in 1986 to its own
building, the History and Political Science Block at the University
campus. Department of History started a diploma program in
Pakistan Studies which was later on upgraded to a regular MA
Pakistan Studies program in 1986. The program of M.Phil. in History
is running since spring 1997, while the Ph.D. program was offered
from its beginning and the Department enrolled Ph.D. students. A
number of scholars have received their Ph.D. degrees from this
department and many other scholars are working on their Ph.D.
projects at the moment. Regular course work for Ph.D. is also going
on. The nomenclature of the Department was changed to
“Department of History & Civilization Studies” in 2016.
The Department came into existence with a staff of three regular
lecturers, one research scholar and one part time teacher. At present,
the Department has the services of five regular teachers including four
Ph.Ds. and one M.Phil. degree holders.

the bifurcation of the Department of Gender Studies and Pakistan

disciplines through an interdisciplinary perspective which focuses on
the significance of gender as a social construct. New scholarly
methods and theories arising from interdisciplinary study encourage
students to examine historical and contemporary representations of
women and men in different walks of life. It fosters scholarly
investigation that recognizes gender as an important stream of reality
that is vital for the establishment of equitable and just society. By
initiating the Gender Studies Program, Bahauddin Zakariya University

this area, to eliminate all forms of violence against women, to remove
the social obstacles in women’s full participation in public life and
decision making at all levels and finally, in the promotion of economic
autonomy of women and their access to resources. The Department is
raising gender consciousness and sensitivity among the people of
Southern Punjab. In this way, the Department develops carring,

The prosperity and success of a nation are always linked to human
resource development, with education being its most crucial aspect. In
line with the University’s vision to meet the educational needs of Southern
Punjab, the Department of Geography was established in 2009, offering
a BS Degree Program in Geography, GIS & Remote Sensing, and
Disaster Management, ADP Geography and Diploma in Geomatics
Geography is a scientific discipline that studies the distribution of natural
and human phenomena on Earth’s surface. It enhances our understanding
of the environment and natural systems, which is essential for
development, improved living conditions, and societal progress. The
field of Geography provides knowledge and skills that contribute to
building an advanced and well-informed society. It involves inquiry,
analysis, and the study of how natural surroundings and geographical
features influence human life.One of the key applications of Geography,
particularly in regions like Southern Punjab, is Disaster Management.
Geographic studies, combined with GIS and Remote Sensing, play a
vital role in disaster preparedness, response, and mitigation. The region’s
diverse landscapes, climate variability, and vulnerability to natural
disasters such as floods, droughts, and heatwaves necessitate a scientific
approach to disaster risk reduction. By integrating Geographic
Information Systems (GIS), early warning systems, and spatial analysis,
Geography helps predict, monitor, and manage disasters effectively,
minimizing loss of life and property.The diversity and richness of
landforms, climate, vegetation, wildlife, and other natural features of
Southern Punjab highlight the importance of Geography in addressing
environmental challenges and disaster resilience. Strengthening expertise

The development and progress of any country is always related to the
development of educational institutions. Throughout the history of
Pakistan this very institution of education established its strength by
introducing behavioral and social sciences that have been diverse in
domain and narrow in focus. Hence, the Department of Sociology
started functioning in 2001 keeping in view the demand of this
discipline in the Southern Punjab. This facility was not previously
available in the entire region. Sociology as an emergent discipline is the
driving force and the main determinant of the development in every
society. Bahauddin Zakariya University Multan has always
contributed to the development, organization and progress of
education and human resource development in Pakistan. Realizing the
significance of this popular social science, the initiative of establishing
the Department of Sociology was taken to address the socio-economic
and cultural issues and their policy implications. Initially, this
department was the part of Institute of Management Sciences (IMS)

Sociology is the study of life focused basically
on how social groups, institutions and society
develop and change. As sociology involves all
types of social relations and its scope is very
broad. Scheme of the program has been designed
to equip the students with professional skills
and knowledge. The curriculum is relevant to
the emerging needs of society.
A career in Sociology would mean the scientific
study of human social behavior and its origin,
development, organization, institution.
Sociology will not only help you comprehend
the human behavior more easily but also know
more but its cause and consequence. Sociology
is more of a subject where the student will have
an eye for detail to understand the behavior of
human beings through their social interactions,
and understand how societies organize, develop
and change.

Philosophy as a discipline deals with the intellectual growth of human
society as an essential process working behind the development of
human understanding and its problems-metaphysical, metaphoric,
Religio-political as well as cultural. This nature of the discipline integrates
philosophy with the other disciplines trying to resolve the problems of
society and expands the scope of philosophy in all walks of life. The
major question for world of knowledge today is how to create a balance
between the traditional and new challenges emerging out of fast growing
world of scientific, Technological, and globalized approaches to
knowledge. The question has made philosophy important for all
methodologies, approaches and mechanisms developed for the growth
of human knowledge.
The history of mankind reveals that there was an immense growth of
philosophical thoughts actually working behind the rise and fall of every
human civilization on the mother earth. Department of philosophy in
Bahauddin Zakariya University, Multan has been established to realize
this importance of the discipline. The department has a commitment to
develop and promote a culture of philosophical also insights and its
education to resolve the socio-political problems not only of the region,
but also at the global level. The department has developed an innovative
scheme of studies encompassing multiple aspects of intellectual concerns
and is trying to connect this scheme of studies with the current problems
of society. The department has developed an understanding of regional
thought patterns as well as the placement of these thoughts in the history
of world philosophy.

The Multan College of Arts (MCA) has undoubtedly emerged as a
significant player in the realm of art and design since its establishment in
2003. Being a pioneering Art and Design institution in the South Punjab
region, its influence extends not only nationally but also internationally,
with former students making their mark in global art communities and
industries. This success is attributed to MCA’s focus on nurturing talent
and providing a platform for both conventional and non-conventional
artistic expression.
One of MCA’s strengths lies in its ability to adapt to the evolving demands
of the art and design markets. By continually updating its curriculum and
course offerings, the college ensures that students are equipped with
the skills and knowledge required to succeed in their respective fields.
The emphasis on practical experience is evident in the college’s state-
of-the-art amenities, including computer labs, art galleries, painting studios,
and drawing studios.
MCA’s commitment to fostering a supportive environment for artistic
exploration is further demonstrated through collaborations such as the
Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Universiti Teknologi Mara,
Malaysia. This agreement facilitates faculty and student exchange
programs, enriching the learning experience and broadening horizons.
Furthermore, the introduction of the M.Phil. program in Art History in
2023 signifies MCA’s dedication to academic excellence and research
in the field of art and design. Looking ahead, the college plans to expand
its offerings with programs like the Bachelor of Craft Design and the
M.Phil. in Art and Design and PhD catering to the evolving needs of the
modern world.
These initiatives are not only beneficial for individual students but also
contribute to the broader development goals of the region, particularly in
South Punjab, where the government places a high priority on education
and skill development. Progress and innovation in the artistic and creative
industries of the region are greatly aided by MCA, as it produces
professionals capable of meeting the needs of the modern world.

Zakariya University, Multan established the Department of Business
Administration in December, 1977 and classes for the first batch
started on March 15, 1978. Institute of Management Sciences
(formerly Department of Business Administration) is now one of the
largest business school of the country with well over 1200 students
and a permanent faculty of 34 teachers with a large complex of
buildings providing all possible facilities at one place. These, together
with the congenial environment offered by a very attractive
University Campus will make most memorable stay at the Campus.
The goal of the Institute is to prepare students for a successful
management career. Since its inception, the Institute has endeavoured
to give its students an education that enables them to face any
challenge in their professional life. Up till now, more than 20000
students have graduated from the Institute who occupy middle and
senior management positions in the hierarchy of national and
multinational organizations in the country.

In 1975, the Government of the Punjab decided to set up four
Engineering Colleges at Taxila, Multan, Faisalabad and Bahawalpur in
the same order of priority. In accordance with the decision of the
Punjab Cabinet, the first Engineering College initially started
functioning at Sahiwal and was later, in 1978, shifted to Taxila as a
second campus of the University of Engineering and Technology,
Lahore. Later its status was raised to an independent University of
Engineering and Technology. The proposal for the second College of
Engineering and Technology at Multan met the approval of the
ECNEC in September 1990.
The College of Engineering and Technology was thus established as a
Constituent College of the Bahauddin Zakariya University, Multan. In
Faculty of Engineering & Technology
2019 its status upgrated to faculty of Engineering & Technology. Its
broad objective is to produce engineers at undergraduate level with
Bachelor’s degree in conventional fields of Civil, Building &
Architectural, Electrical, Computer, Mechanical, Metallurgy &
Materials and Textile Engineering to meet the engineering manpower
requirements of the province/country.
The Faculty of Engineering & Technology offers courses leading to
the award of 4-Year engineering degree in Civil, Electrical, Building &
Architectural, Computer, Mechanical, Metallurgy & Materials and
Textile Engineering. The Faculty of Engineering & Technology

Introduction
The Department of Building & Architectural Engineering was
established in Baha Ud-din Zakariya University in 2004. Initially it
offered 5-year BSc Building & Architectural Engineering Program.
However, in 2009, the program duration was reduced to 4-year to
comply with the Pakistan Engineering Council (PEC) requirements.
Since then the department is offering 4-year BSc program in Building
& Architectural Engineering.
The Building & Architectural Engineering program is a blend of
Architecture and Civil Engineering with emphasis to impart quality
education to the students and prepare them for the building industry
of Pakistan. The graduates of our department are working in various
national and international organizations. The curriculum of the
program is designed to equip the graduates with architectural design,
building structural design, building services design (e.g. HVAC
systems, electrical systems in buildings, lighting & illumination, fire
safety, acoustics and plumbing) with strong knowledge of
construction materials, construction techniques, construction
management and conservation of heritage buildings.
Department Vision
“To impart quality education in Building & Architectural
Engineering with innovative & multi-disciplinary approach for
providing sustainable solutions to meet the requirements of
building industry and societal benefits”
Department Mission
“To produce competent professionals for local and global building
industry capable to meet emerging challenges of building sector
with architectural and engineering knowledge of building systems
and related research”

INTRODUCTION:
As per the vision of the Punjab Government
and following the approval from the Executive
Committee of the National Economic Council
(ECNEC) in 1990, the Mechanical Engineering
Department (MED) was established in 2004
as part of the University College of Engineering
and Technology. At the time of its inception, it
was the only department in South Punjab
offering a B.Sc. degree in Mechanical
Engineering.
Initially, the program followed an annual
assessment system, which was later upgraded
to a term system, and subsequently to the
semester system. In alignment with the latest
advancements in educational practices, the
department has successfully implemented the
Outcome-Based Education (OBE) system
within the semester framework. Currently, the
B.Sc. Mechanical Engineering degree is
accredited by the Pakistan Engineering
Council (PEC) at Level-II under the
Washington Accord.
The department comprises 14 permanent
faculty members, of whom 10 hold Ph.D.
degrees, while one faculty member is currently
enrolled in a Ph.D. program. Additionally, there
are 4 Lab Engineers who support students
with hands-on training using the latest
mechanical engineering equipment and software
tools.
The curriculum is designed in accordance with
the latest field requirements and the criteria set
by HEC and PEC. It includes specialized
courses in Thermal Power, Design, Artificial
Intelligence, Manufacturing, Engineering
Mechanics, Robotics and Automation, as well
as interdisciplinary, natural sciences, and
management courses to equip students with
the latest tools and techniques in mechanical
engineering.
In 2021, the department launched a
postgraduate program (MS in Mechanical
Engineering) aimed at fostering a research-
oriented academic environment. The primary
goal of this research-based program is to
develop practical solutions to engineering
challenges faced by the global community. The
department also plans to commence its Ph.D.
program in the near future.

innovate and advance sustainable technologies.

progress and achieve global recognition under

Introduction:
The Department of Computer Engineering is
established in 2004 under the Faculty of
Engineering and Technology by Bahauddin
Zakariya University, Multan. Computer
Engineering programs are accredited by the
Pakistan Engineering Council (PEC). The
modern era has witnessed a rapid development
in computer Engineering, both in hardware and
software. Each year a host of new
advancements is unveiled, from home robotics
to advanced operating systems,
microprocessors, and supercomputers with
massive computational capabilities. Computer
Engineers are responsible for the design and
development of certain pieces of technology
that are used every day. From personal
computers and desktops to smartphones and
robotics, these advancements in technology are
meant to add convenience to our daily lives.
Computer Engineering principles can be applied
to a number of other purposes, including the
development of integrated circuits, embedded

Introduction
The city of Multan is the center of the cotton production of Southern
Punjab. There was a need for an institute that could provide skilled and
technically trained manpower to the local textile industry. The Export
Promotion Bureau (EPB) in collaboration with Multan Textile Education
Trust took the initiative and founded the Institute of Handloom and
Home Textile Technology (IHHTT).
In 2004, Bahauddin Zakariya University (BZU) took over control of
the institute, and a degree program for Textile Engineering was launched.
Four specializations, namely, Yarn Manufacturing, Fabric Manufacturing,
Textile Chemistry and Garments Manufacturing are being offered. The
number of seats in 4 specializations varies each year to reflect the changing
trends and demand of the local market. The syllabi have been designed to
impart student’s firm grip not only on engineering concepts but also to
enhance management capabilities. Out of 136credit hours offered, 43 are
non-engineeringthat include natural sciences, management sciences
computer sciences and humanities whereas 93 areengineering domain.
Being a textile leader ofthe south Punjab region, the College of Textile
Engineering has launched a new degree program “BS Textile Design” on
the huge demand of the export industry. This program generates human
resources in the field of design with intense knowledge of textiles. In
addition, it also strengthens the design houses and textile industry to
develop new products with creative designs and contribute to

Dean’s Message
As the Dean of the Faculty of Islamic Studies and Languages at Bahauddin Zakariya University, it is my distinct pleasure to
welcome you to an institution dedicated to excellence in scholarship, cultural understanding, and personal growth. Our
Faculty stands at the crossroads of tradition and innovation, committed to nurturing a generation of scholars and leaders who
are well-equipped to engage with the complexities of the modern world while upholding the rich heritage of Islamic thought
and linguistic diversity.
At Bahauddin Zakariya University, we recognize the profound significance of Islamic Studies and Languages in shaping both
historical consciousness and contemporary dialogues. Our specialized programs in Islamic theologyas well as advanced
language studies including Arabic, English, Saraiki, and Urduare meticulously designed to offer students a comprehensive
understanding of Islamic studies and literature, alongside a deep appreciation for the intricacies of languages.
The Faculty of Islamic Studies and Languages is distinguished by its dedicated faculty members, each a leading scholar in
their respective areas. Our educators bring a wealth of knowledge, experience, and passion to the classroom, fostering an
environment where critical thinking and intellectual curiosity are paramount. Through dynamic lectures, interactive seminars,
research opportunities as well as cultural and literary events, our students are prepared to contribute meaningfully to
academic discourse and societal progress.
As you consider your future at Bahauddin Zakariya University, I encourage you to reflect on the values of intellectual rigor,

Since its formation in 1975, the Department of English continues to
enjoy excellent repute, setting up high standards of academic excellence
and innovation. Employing a significant number of PhD and Post-doc
faculty members, the Department of English has been committed to the
goal of delivering quality education by combining the latest knowledge
in the fields of literature and linguistics with a learning atmosphere that
fosters creativity and critical thinking. Believing in the dictum of
education/learning with responsibility, the courses taught at Department
of English not only educate its students in the study of literary giants
like William Shakespeare, John Milton, William Wordsworth, Jane
Austen, T.S. Eliot, Virginia Woolf, and Robert Frost, these courses also
employ contemporary literary and theoretical frameworks to engage
with the present-day intra/international geo-political and socio-economic
concerns like wars, genocide, economic disparity, violence, globalization,
colonization, and women’s issues. Taking a multi-disciplinary approach
to the teaching of literature(s) in English, the Department of English also
has the distinct honour of being home to some of the leading voices in the
field of linguistics. Given the increasing application of linguistics in
modern technologies and media discourses, our courses in linguistics are
continually updated to keep at par with the demands of this emergent
market. The in-house departmental library equipped with the latest
books in the field of linguistics and English language teaching, in particular,
is a testament to this comittment.

The faculty at Department of English comprises of a significant number
of foreign-qualified teachers, who have had the privilege of studying at
some of the top-class universities of the world (including the USA and
UK) by winning prestigious awards including Fulbright, Commonwealth
and the HEC scholarships. The Department of English offers a wide
range of courses, both in literature as well as linguistics, through a variety
of degree programs and short courses ranging from BS to PhD. The
students are continuously engaged and challenged through a host of
curricular and co/extra-curricular activities such as quizes, seminars,
dramatic activities, tutorials and conferences. The students of our
Department have access to the Higher Education Commission’s digital
library, an in-house departmental library and the Lincoln Corner,
established inside the University’s Central Library.
The Department’s academic richness results in the production of quality
human resources. Our graduates play a vital role in the socio-economic
development of the country. Similarly, they have valuable
accomplishments to their credit in foreign lands. Common professions
they pursue include Teaching and Research, Civil Services (through CSS),
Provincial Management Services (PMS/former PCS), Media, Armed

Becoming a Call Center’s representative, or a Content Writer (in the

where our graduates have been able to successfully apply their skills.
Moreover, Middle East’s educational institutions attract our graduates
through handsome packages. It is relevant to mention that many of our

Sufism, also known as Tasawwuf, a mystical
dimension of Islam. It emerged in the 8th
century CE, primarily in present-day Iran, Iraq,
and Central Asia.Sufism and Mysticism have a
rich history that spans over 1,400 years, with
roots in Islamic spirituality. Early Sufis sought
a more personal and intimate connection with
Allah.Sufism emphasizes the importance of
spiritual guidance, meditation, contemplation,
and devotional rituals and commitment to
ethical and moral values. The ultimate goal is
to become a true servant of Almighty ALLAH,
living a life of love, compassion and service to
all of his creations.
The Institute of Sufism & Mysticism
Bahauddin Zakariya University, Multan
attempts to promote a moderate and responsible
style of discourse on the issues concerning
contemporary understanding of Islam and the
challenges that are faced by the humanity in
general and Muslim World in particular.The
Institute pays special attention to developing
contact with relevant scholars and institutions
across the globe for advancing research and
studies in the field. Aims to publish
monographs, books, research reports and other
material deemed to be necessary for developing
Knowledge of the discipline.
Higher Education Commission, Islamabad
directed Bahauddin Zakariya University
Multan for establishment of Institute of Sufism
& Mysticism in 2021. Currently Institute of
Sufism & Mysticism is working in Bahauddin
Zakariya University Multan under the
Supervision of Prof. Dr. Abdul Quddus Suhaib
as first project Director.
The Institute is aimed and objected to:
1. Provide opportunities of credible studies
and research in a conducive atmosphere.
2. Collect relevant data on Sufism and allied
Knowledge and facilitate the scholars to conduct
research in this field.
3. Develop a methodology for research in the
various fields of Sufism and Islamic learning,
to identify and study contemporary problems
and interpret the teachings of Islam in order to
assist the Pakistani society and Muslim World
in particular and globe in general.
4. Conduct National and International
Seminars, Conferences and workshops to
achieve and promote its objectives.
5. Initiate a research journal for advancing
knowledge of the field.
6. Expand linkages with the national and
international institutions and renowned persons
working in the discipline.

The establishment of Saraiki Area Study Centre (SASC) in Bahauddin
Zakariya University was the outcome of the new perspectives on the
Southern Punjab/ Saraiki Region with Multan as its political, intellectual
and cultural nucleus. The Saraiki Research Centre (SRC) was established
in 2001. A few important research projects were completed and a number
of books were published under its umbrella.
Soon it was converted into the Department of Saraiki in May 2006,
and the regular classes of ADA/ADS. (5th Semester) Saraiki were started
accordingly. The Saraiki Region, being a part of the vast area of the
ancient Indus Valley Civilization, owns rich traditions of language,
literature, culture, history and archaeology etc. Saraiki is the ancient
native language of the Southern Punjab and several districts of Sindh,
Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with centuries old shared
traditions of literature and cultural activities.
The ex-Prime-Minister Syed Yousuf Raza Gillani inaugurated the Saraiki
Area Study Centre on 23rd January 2010. Earlier, the honorable Prime
Minister had announced the grant of 30 million rupees for the
strengthening and the development of the SASC. A commemorative
book “Saraiki Wasaib” was also published on this occasion.
It is worth mentioning that following four new academic departments
have been also approved in the scheme of SASC:
1. Department of Archaeology
2. Department of Cultural Studies
3. Department of Linguistic Communication
4. Department of Post-Colonial Studies
5. Khawaja Ghulam Fareed Chair
Saraiki Area Study Centre (SASC)
The Department of Saraiki (established in 2006) is already functioning
with its regular classes as the premier department of the SASC in its
elegant new building. The syllabus of ADA/ADS. (5th Semester) Saraiki
is designed with inter-disciplinary approach so that its graduates may

As the Dean of Faculty of Pharmacy, I am honored to highlight the vital role of pharmacy in shaping healthcare and
improving lives. Pharmacy is a comprehensive field that ensures the safe, effective and ethical use of drugs, contributing
to disease prevention, treatment, and overall well-being.There are different branches of pharmacy each play a crucial
role in advancing healthcare: Pharmaceutical Chemistry focuses on drug discovery, development and ensuring the safety
and efficacy of medicines. Pharmaceutics involves the formulation and delivery of drugs, optimizing how medications are
absorbed and utilized by the body. Pharmacology studies the effects of drugs on biological systems, helping to develop
safer and more effective treatments. Pharmacy Practice ensures that medications are prescribed, dispensed, and used
appropriately, enhancing patient care and safety. Pharmacognosy explores natural medicinal compounds derived from
plants and other sources, contributing to the discovery of new therapeutic agents. Pharmacy professionals play an
indispensable role in hospitals, research labs, the pharmaceutical industry, and community health, working to improve
medication access, educate patients, and drive medical innovation. As healthcare continues to evolve, the importance of
pharmacy and its various disciplines grows even stronger, ensuring a healthier and more informed society.

Introduction
Department of Pharmacognosy in the Faculty of Pharmacy, Bahuddin
Zakariya University Multan, was established in October 2017. Its
background refers to the traditional history of more than ten centuries.
Pharmacognosy is the science of bioactive natural substances found in
plants, animals, microbes, minerals and recently marine organisms.
Researchers in this field investigate natural compounds, new therapeutic
agents, biological activities of the substances obtained from natural
sources, herb-drug interactions and phytotherapy. The Department is
well equipped with an undergraduate research laboratory, a crude drug
museum, herbarium specimen of several plant materials and modern

products.

The Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry was re-established in
October 2017, under the Faculty of Pharmacy, BZU, Multan and
specializes in Natural Product Chemistry, Synthetic Chemistry, and
Drug Design. The Department offers M.Phil. In Pharmaceutical
Chemistry and Ph.D. in Pharmaceutical Chemistry, both recognized
by the Higher Education Commission (HEC). Faculty members are
engaged in multidisciplinary research projects funded by national and
international agencies. Students are trained in advanced techniques
such as spectroscopic analysis, molecular docking and structural
elucidation, which strengthens their skills and confidence as young
scientists. The department takes pride in publishing research articles
in reputed journals and in producing graduates who are contributing to
academia, pharmaceutical industries and research institution across
Pakistan and abroad.
An air-conditioned library with adequate collection of 881 text books,
reference books and research journals has been established at the
Department/Faculty covering various disciplines of Pharmacy. The books
are also available to research students from the Book Bank of the
University on loan basis total 881 books are available for the subject of
Pharmaceutical Chemistry. Internet facilities in computer lab is available
for maintaining high standards of education in Pharmacy.
The students during the course of their studies go on industrial tours of
various Pharmaceutical industries and laboratories as a part of their
practical/professional training and skill development. The Department
has liaison with different employing organization and Pharmaceutical
Institutions which facilitate the students seeking employment.
Gold Medal is awarded to the student getting first position in M. Phil.
Pharmaceutical Chemistry.
The Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry has a collection of over
881 specialized textbooks, reference books, and research journals,
covering diverse discipline of Pharmaceutical Chemistry including organic

chemistry. To support advanced research and education, an E-Library is
available, ensuring seamless connectivity to scientific databases and digital
resources, thereby maintaining high academic and research standards in
Pharmacy.
Industrial Tours
The students during M.Phil. and Ph.D. visits to various pharmaceutical
industries and research laboratories as part of their advanced practical
training/professional & skill development. The Department maintains
strong collaborations with leading pharmaceutical organizations and
research institutions, providing scholars with opportunities for
networking, skill enhancement, and potential employment avenues.
Merit Awards
Gold Medal is awarded to the student getting first position in M.

Laboratory Facilities
The Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry features Two state-of-
the-art Natural Product Chemistry laboratories for M.Phil. and Ph.D.
equipped with the following instruments:
 	High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC)
 	Rotary Evaporator
 	Fraction Collector
 	Freeze Dryer
 	Filtration Pump
 	Digital and Electronic Spectrophotometers
 	Fluorescence Spectrophotometer
 	Fourier Transform Infrared Spectrometer (FTIR)

Computer-Aided Drug Design (CADD) Facility
The Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry hosts a modern Computer-
Aided Drug Design (CADD) Facility dedicated to advanced drug
discovery research. The facility utilizes state-of-the-art software,
including Gaussian for DFT studies, Glide for molecular docking, and
GROMACS for Molecular Dynamics simulations. Advanced QSAR
modeling techniques are employed to predict and optimize biological
activity of drug candidates. Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial
Intelligence (AI) tools are integrated for virtual screening, drug
repurposing, and predictive modeling. These computational approaches
accelerate the identification and development of novel therapeutic agents.
The facility provides a strong platform for postgraduate research,
innovation, and interdisciplinary collaboration in pharmaceutical sciences.

Welcome to the Centre for Advanced Studies in Pure and Applied
Mathematics (CASPAM), Bahauddin Zakariya University, Multan —
one of the leading institutions in Pakistan for higher education and research
in Mathematics and its modern applications.We are delighted that you
are considering pursuing your academic journey with us. CASPAM
offers a dynamic and intellectually stimulating environment where
students are empowered to develop strong analytical, computational,
and problem-solving skills essential for academia, industry, business,
finance, data science, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.The
following sections provide an overview of CASPAM, including our
academic programs, distinguished faculty, research opportunities, modern
infrastructure, computational facilities, and vibrant academic community
dedicated to excellence in teaching, learning, innovation, and research.
Introduction
CASPAM envisions achieving excellence in teaching, learning, research,
and innovation by developing intellectually strong, professionally
competent, ethically responsible, and socially impactful individuals
capable of contributing to academia, industry, and society.
With the motto “Mathematics for Industry, Society and Humanity,”
CASPAM is committed to promoting interdisciplinary education and
research through the integration of Pure, Applied, Computational,
Financial, and Industrial Mathematics with emerging fields such as
Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Machine Learning, Informatics,
Information Technology, and Business Analytics. The Centre strives to
produce highly skilled human resources capable of addressing modern
scientific, technological, industrial, and societal challenges.
CASPAM has established a distinguished reputation for academic
excellence, quality research, and holistic student development. Highly
qualified faculty members with strong professional and ethical values, a
supportive and intellectually stimulating academic environment,
innovative and technology-enabled teaching methodologies, outcome-
based education, state-of-the-art infrastructure, active student
engagement, and strong academia–industry linkages collectively make
CASPAM an exceptional institution for undergraduate and graduate
studies.
The Centre strongly believes in nurturing creativity, innovation,

so that they may contribute effectively toward technological

of humanity.
At CASPAM, we recognize the increasing importance of Mathematics
in the modern world, particularly its central role in Artificial Intelligence,
Data Science, Financial Analytics, Machine Learning, Scientific
Computing, Decision Sciences, Business Analytics and emerging
technologies associated with Industrial Revolutions 4.0 and 5.0. Our
academic programs are therefore designed to combine strong mathematical
foundations with modern computational and analytical skills aligned
with global technological and sustainable development goals.
CASPAM offers BS, MS/MPhil, and PhD programs in Mathematics,
BS Financial Analytics (jointly with the Department of Commerce), BS
Artificial Intelligence (jointly with the Department of Computer Science)
and BS Data Science (jointly with the Department of Computer Science
CASPAM
and the Department of Statistics). These programs are integrated with
modern areas of specialization. These programs provide students with
opportunities for intellectual growth, scientific exploration, advanced
research, and professional development while enabling them to pursue
diverse career pathways in academia, industry, finance, technology,
business, and research organizations.
Our study programs emphasize critical thinking, quantitative reasoning,
mathematical modeling, computational problem solving, algorithmic
development, analytical decision-making, and real-world applications.
Students are trained to analyze complex systems, interpret data, formulate
mathematical models, and develop innovative solutions to challenges
arising in science, engineering, economics, finance, business, and
technology. By staying up-to-date with the latest developments in
Mathematics, our programs ensure that students are well-prepared to
tackle real-world challenges and contribute to the advancement of the
discipline. This makes them capable of finding roles such as data scientists,
actuaries, business and financial analysts, industrial researchers and
problem-solvers in the areas of design, analysis, optimization and
automation.
Graduates of CASPAM are successfully serving in federal and provincial

The Computer Centre at CASPAM serves as a hub for computational

The Institute of Computing came into existence in April 2009, as an up-

environment that aims at bringing out the best in the knowledge-seekers.
As the computing industry matured, professional qualifications are

the recommendation of IEEE and ACM joint committee on Computer
Science Curriculum and also conforms to the recommendations of the
National Curriculum Revision Committee in the Information
Technology, Computer Science and Telecommunication Systems, duly
approved by the Higher Education Commission, Ministry of Education
and Ministry of Science and Technology.
The students in the Institute of Computing have almost unlimited access
to computers and the professional software tools that go with them. The
Institute has over 10 teaching laboratories/interactive classrooms, which
are equipped with more than 400 Dual Core based multimedia PCs loaded
with Windows, Linux, Sun V890 Server, Sun StorEdge 6610 SAN and Sun
Ultra Sparc Enterprise System with 40 Sun Ray-I workstations. All these
teaching laboratories/interactive classrooms are networked to 10
common Dual/Quad Xeon based servers. They are also connected to the
university Fiber Optic based Campus LAN and to the outside world via
HEC PERN-1 & PERN-2 network. Each of them is fitted with an
overhead multimedia projector. The Institute also has the facility of
Video Conferencing Room funded by the HEC, which will provide an
opportunity of access and connectivity for the University to the human
resource across the globe. It will help to boost the level of academic and
research activity.

entire university. Firstly, the Institute of Computing is looking after the
huge Fiber Optic based Campus LAN. Secondly, the official website of
the University is also being maintained by the Institute. Thirdly, Internet

The Department of Statistics is one of the pioneering departments of
the University, established in 1975 alongside the founding of Bahauddin
Zakariya University. It began its operations in a rented building in
Gulgasht Colony Multan before relocating to the “Statistics and
Mathematics Block” on the main campus in 1987. Today, the Department
operates from its own dedicated building, adjacent to the original block.
Despite its modest beginnings, the Department has grown into one of
the leading institutions for statistical education in Pakistan, comparable
to any top-ranking university in the country. It boasts a highly qualified
faculty of 11 members, all of whom hold Ph.D. degrees, ensuring
excellence in teaching and research.
Statistics forms the backbone of quantitative reasoning and data-driven
decision-making, providing essential tools to solve complex problems
across diverse fields. It empowers intelligent data collection, rigorous
analysis, and meaningful interpretation-critical for informed choices in
economics, business, public policy, and scientific research. From medicine
and bioinformatics to forensics and image reconstruction, statistical
methods bridge disciplines, transforming raw data into actionable insights.
As the demand for skilled statisticians continues to surge, the discipline
stands unique in its ability to unify science, industry, and policy through
the universal language of data.

Introduction
Molecular Biology and Biotechnology is defined as the application
ofscientific and engineering principles to the processing of materials by
biological agents to produce goods and services. The completion of human
genome and Arabidopsis genome projects in the year 2000 were great
break through in the field of biotechnology. In the last twenty years,
unprecedented progress in Molecular Biology and Biotechnology has
been observed, which has made revolutionary impacts on every aspect
of human activity such as agriculture, forestry, horticulture, livestock,
health, medicine and environment. In agriculture, it is predicted that the

be due to the biotechnological innovations. In livestock, production of
new transgenic animals will not only meet the future needs of protein,
dairy products etc.but these animals could also be used as bioreactor for
the production of various pharmaceutical products. New safe protein
drugs, particularly by site-directed mutagenesis, vaccines, diagnostic
kits, antibiotics and enzymes can be produced by exploiting the
Biotechnology in the field of medicine (Medical Biotechnology). The
genetic based diagnostic assays for some genetic disorders and other
diseases have already been developed and their treatment by gene therapy
would be possible.
The primary objective of the Institute of Molecular Biology and
Biotechnology (IMBB) is to produce man power that can contribute to
the development of Pakistan, particularly in science and technologyand
its economy in general.
